A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RILKE under the same title and authorship. All pages, including the appendices, are readable, and the text, equations, tables and figures support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original UnKE and EditEverything experiments, MMLU evaluations, intervention ablations, routing measurements and inference-latency results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds ZsRE evaluation, baseline comparisons, hard-negative analysis, radius sensitivity, router activation checks and training-cost measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 change the specified individual and cluster routing rules from minimizing squared Euclidean distance to maximizing cosine similarity. The intervention map, KL-regularized objective and clustering procedure remain unchanged. The relevance gate newly explained in the method section was already present in v1 Section 5.2.

E1.justification: v2 extends evaluation from unstructured editing on UnKE and EditEverything to structured editing on ZsRE. It also tests lexically similar, semantically different hard negatives within UnKE. These extend task and test-scenario coverage; the original datasets and MMLU evaluation remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GRACE for both models, adds WISE to the Qwen comparison, and removes LoRA from the Llama comparison despite retaining its appendix description. Table 2 narrows the resource comparison by removing AnyEdit, UnKE and MEMIT, retaining WISE. The EditEverything comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 3,000-edit ZsRE protocol with reliability, generalization, locality and average scores; lexical-similarity-based hard-negative selection; and router checks using 1,000 paraphrases and 5,000 MMLU queries. Resource evaluation changes from parameter counts to storage costs and adds training-time/peak-memory measurements. The retained UnKE batch size, temperature and gating threshold are unchanged, while the reported checkpoints omit T=1.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of semantic locality against hard negatives (A.1), radius-induced interference (A.6.2), and relevant versus irrelevant router activation (A.7.1). It removes v1 A.1's forgetting analysis over 100 edits in batches of 10. The loss ablation, layer study, cluster-threshold analysis, routing-scalability study and generated-answer cases are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions use point estimates and empirical distributions, including the same spread annotations in Figure 1. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new hard-negative means and medians summarize added analysis results without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Retained UnKE, EditEverything and Tables 3–4 scores are unchanged. v2 adds baseline rows and ZsRE results, including RILKE averages of 0.88 on Llama and 0.85 on Qwen, while removing LoRA and T=1 results. It replaces parameter-count results with storage costs and adds radius, routing and training-cost outcomes, including 58 seconds per edit and 19 GB peak memory. These are newly reported results, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The formal routing definitions in Sections 4.2–4.3 change from squared-L2 minimization to cosine maximization, which are not equivalent as written without normalization assumptions. The two geometric properties, ReFT map, robustness derivation, clustering algorithm and routing-accuracy definition otherwise remain substantively unchanged; no new proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same central contributions: robust representation interventions, query-adaptive routing and shared-subspace control for scalable lifelong knowledge editing. The additional evaluations support these claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations distinguishing semantic routing from lexical matching, explaining interference at larger perturbation radii, and attributing narrower ZsRE advantages to shorter generation requirements. It also argues for protection through query rejection and limited effects of false activation. New Section 9 explicitly acknowledges untested extreme-scale knowledge bases and unassessed adversarial-editing and bias risks.

D1.justification: Table 8 newly specifies learning rate 0.01, 1,000 epochs, radius 0.02 and maximum cluster size 16, while consolidating the previously indicated rank and intervention layer. v2 also specifies fp32 for storage reporting and supplies training-time measurements. These fill important reproducibility gaps without establishing that existing training settings changed. The EasyEdit and Gemini access pointers remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations concerning activation steering, ZsRE and editing risks, including Rimsky et al., Levy et al., BadEdit and ripple-effect evaluation, while removing the SheetDesigner and predictive-analysis citations. Its central positioning relative to weight-space and representation-based editing remains stable. Updated Qwen metadata and duplicate GRACE/Geometry of Truth entries do not constitute distinct new works.

P1.justification: Substantial paragraph rewriting spans the abstract, introduction, motivation, method, experiments and related work. Section 3 is reorganized around semantic locality and the geometric properties. v2 adds a limitations section and reorganizes appendix material into cost, configuration and routing subsections, moving the layer study out of the main text.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned for ZsRE and revised comparators, and Table 2 becomes a storage comparison. v2 adds cost, configuration and radius tables plus a hard-negative figure, redraws the framework and PCA illustrations, relocates the layer figure and removes the forgetting figure. Much of the appendix changes from full-width prose to two-column layout.

improvement.justification: v1's locality evidence primarily used random-pair separation and retained MMLU performance; v2 directly examines lexical confounding and router rejection. Together with the GRACE and Qwen-WISE comparisons, radius analysis and newly disclosed training settings, this substantially strengthens validation and reproducibility of the existing framework. Explicit limitations better bound its applicability. Removing the single-edit results and forgetting curve reduces some evidence, but the retained sequential evaluations preserve support for the main lifelong-editing claims.
